newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Emerging Europe Advertising & Media Digest-July 1.
newsitem.headline: Emerging Europe Advertising & Media Digest-July 1.

text.p: REUTERS EMERGING EUROPE PRESS DIGEST FOR ADVERTISING & MEDIA
Weekly Press Digest from Central and Eastern Europe on Advertising, Marketing, the Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Markets
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

-- Makers of feminine hygiene products spent 200 million crowns ($6.2 million) on advertising in the Czech Republic last year. The largest advertiser was Procter & Gamble, which spent 42 million crowns advertising the Always brand. (Strategie News, June 18-25, 1997)
-- Advertising spend by Polish companies grew 50 percent in 1996, significantly exceeding industry expectations, Marek Janicki president of ad agency ITI/McCann-Erickson says.
(Rzeczpospolita, June 26, 1997)
-- The Hungarian Parliament passes an advertising bill that while widely welcomed by advertisers and ad agencies, opposition parties say is far too liberal. (Vilaggazdasag, June 26, 1997)
-- Advertising on public transport is developing fast in Russia, and the number of agencies specialising in this area has increased threefold. (Finansoviye Izvestiya, June 25, 1997)

-- Media buying company Mediapolis announces it handled 120 million zlotys ($36.7 million) worth of business and was the most successful media buyer in Poland last year. (Businessman Magazine, June 1997)
-- Azerbaijan's parliament has amended its law on advertising to include some restrictions on alcohol and tobacco advertising.
(Panorama, June 27, 1997)
-- Bulgaria's Association of Advertising Agencies says it has set up a commission which would prepare an advertising draft law by the end of the year. (Capital, June 23-29, 1997)
-- Two market research firms, CASE and J. Walter Thompson/Parintex, have developed a programme which profiles 46,531 Polish consumers. (Businessman Magazine, June 1997)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:
-- Cash-strapped Bulgarian National Television will cut its staff by 30 percent in September as a part of a restructuring programme aimed to cut losses. (Kontinent, June 24, 1997)

-- According to the first official results from the "peoplemeters" which are measuring Czech television viewing, the Nova Television channel is watched the most. The most popular programmes were the Sunday news show Televizni Noviny and the American serial Dallas, which was watched by more than three million viewers. The "peoplemeters" are being used in 660 households. (Pravo, June 24, 1997)
-- The Czech daily newspaper Lidove Noviny is introducing
changes to give it a a more professional image. Its profits from advertisements last year were 64.6 million crowns ($2 million).
(Strategie News, June 18-25, 1997)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS, MARKETS & CONSUMER TRENDS:

-- Levi's stores in the Czech Republic are running an unusual promotion for Levi 501 Shrink-To-Fit, "wet jeans". Models sit in baths of water in the stores to demonstrate to consumers how the jeans shrink to fit. (Strategie News, June 18-25, 1997)
-- The use of pirated software in Poland declined to 71 percent
from 77 percent from 1994 to 1996, the Business Software Alliance says. (Dziennik Prawa i Gospodarki, 26 June 1997)
-- Restaurant company American Bistro Poland plans to invest up
to $9.0 million in six TGI Friday restaurants in the next 18 months. The restaurants will target consumers on average
incomes. (Puls Biznesu, June 26, 1997)
-- The Greek airline Olympic Airways has signed a co-operation
agreement with the Hungarian carrier Malev Rt. There will now be
five regular flights between Athens and Budapest every week
(Vilaggazdasag, June 24, 1997)
-- France's Thomson Multimedia will invest 170 million French
francs ($29 million) in a television assembly plant in Zyrardow,
central Poland. (Rzeczpospolita, June 26, 1997)
-- Most Poles prefer Polish beer brands, followed by German, Czech and Dutch beers, a consumer survey by the Pentor polling institute finds. (Puls Biznesu, June 26, 1997)
-- Hungarian car maker Magyar Suzuki Rt plans to increase production by 10 percent this year to 60,000 cars.
(Vilaggazdasag, June 25, 1997)

-- Hungarian beer producers have to spend an increasing amount on advertising because beer consumption is declining and consumers are not loyal to individual brands, industry experts say. Last year the Hungarian beer industry spent a total of 408 million forints ($2.2 million) on advertising. (Vilaggazdasag,
-- Supermarket chain Austria Spar International plans to open 12 new supermarkets in Hungary in the near future. It aims to
become one of the top three retailers in the country.
(Vilaggazdasag, June 25, 1997)
-- Procter & Gamble introduces a new hairspray, Pantene Elastesse, on the Czech market. (Strategie News, June 18-25,
